questions.q: Why is a PostgreSQL major-version upgrade generally a bigger event than a SQL Server version update, per this lesson?
options: PostgreSQL's on-disk data format can change between major versions, so new binaries generally can't just start up against the old data directory
PostgreSQL has no concept of version numbers
SQL Server never changes its on-disk format between versions either, making the two identical
PostgreSQL requires a full operating system reinstall for every major version
questions.explain: Because the on-disk format can differ across major versions, the data must be converted or reloaded, which is why PostgreSQL provides dedicated upgrade tooling.

questions.q: What is the key difference between pg_upgrade's copy mode and link mode?
options: Copy mode copies data files and keeps the old cluster as a fallback; link mode hard-links files for speed but removes the old cluster as an independent fallback
Copy mode is faster than link mode in every case
Link mode performs a full logical dump and reload, while copy mode does not touch the data at all
Copy mode only works for minor version upgrades, not major ones
questions.explain: Copy mode is safer but slower since it copies every data file; link mode hard-links files for speed but sacrifices the old cluster as a rollback option.

questions.q: Why can logical replication be used for a near-zero-downtime PostgreSQL major-version migration?
options: A logical subscriber doesn't need to match the publisher's PostgreSQL major version, so a new-version cluster can catch up while the old one keeps serving traffic
Logical replication automatically performs an in-place binary upgrade with zero configuration
It replicates the entire cluster byte-for-byte faster than pg_upgrade
It requires no additional cluster and runs entirely within the existing data directory
questions.explain: Because logical replication tolerates version differences between publisher and subscriber, a new-version cluster can be kept current via subscription until cutover, avoiding a long maintenance window.

questions.q: What extra operational complexity does the logical-replication migration approach commit a DBA to, compared to pg_upgrade?
options: Running and monitoring two clusters side by side, including watching replication lag before cutover
There is no added complexity — it is strictly simpler than pg_upgrade in every respect
It requires disabling all client connections to the old cluster during the entire migration
It eliminates the need for any testing before migration
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly notes that logical replication migration means running two clusters side by side and dealing with logical replication's known limits (DDL, sequences) before cutover.

Lesson 85 repeats the same PostgreSQL replication content from a different angle
